reason: Citation is verbatim correct: SetupWizard.java:2171-2175 is `case "setup-reset": player.closeInventory(); s.step = 1; showStep(player, s);` and the four required-field bounces at 2140, 2148, 2155, 2162 likewise assign s.step then call showStep. showStep (306-322) only clears villager previews and dispatches to showStepXxx; none of showStepWorld/Core/Spawns/Nodes/Villagers/Shop/Preview (325-330, 343-347, 371-379, 593, 873, 896, 938) writes wizard.step, so there is no hidden persistence the finding missed. Persistence really is asymmetric: goto persists explicitly (1645-1646 `s.step = targetStep; autoSaveSilent(player);`) and validateCompletion's identical bounce persists with a comment explaining exactly why (1200-1203 "否则 config.yml 里可能残留 step=8 的旧值...此刻重启会再次落到 8"), which proves the author's own contract that a bounce must be flushed. start() does honor the stale value: 240 `int savedStep = plugin.getConfig().getInt("wizard.step." + player.getUniqueId(), 0);` then 248-259 assigns session.step = savedStep and calls sendResuming/showStep without any 'resume flag'. So the defect is real and reachable (step 7 is reachable via /hilltop setup preview, which itself writes step=7 at 1601-1603, so config holds 7 when [Reset Setup] sets the session to 1). It is downgraded rather than confirmed because the harm is bounded to a wrong step pointer: no deployment data is deleted by the reset anyway (P2-4 at 1243-1248 deliberately preserves core), the admin gets an explicit 'setup.resuming' banner naming step and arena (266-273), and one more click on the still-present [Reset Setup] or any subsequent autoSave-bearing action (e.g. confirm-world at 1249-1251) re-flushes the value. The narrow window is 'reset/bounce then quit with no intervening saved action'.
